routing.ruling: Curriculum, not reference. The overview and ten unit guides form one coherent Grade 2 Spanish reading workshop with a 30-week scope, recurring daily routines, model texts, essential questions, assessment, vocabulary reinforcement, and 150 ordered minilessons. Those teach a sequence and method, so the five curriculum layers are the correct ingestion surface.
routing.recipeRuling: The repeatable parent-facing surfaces resolve to existing Homa recipes: reading-comprehension-mini-unit, lesson-comprehension-check, guided-notes, checklist-assessment, classification-sorting-mat, unit-study-packet, notes-and-practice-bundle, and reader-theater-script. Classroom talk and conferencing are preserved as method adaptations, not invented as printable-format gaps.

layer1_philosophy.methodology: Content-rich reading workshop with brief explicit modeling, guided practice, independent transfer, observational adjustment, collaborative talk, and recurring vocabulary and assessment routines
principles: Build reading comprehension and academic vocabulary through ten coherent knowledge themes rather than unrelated passages.
Open with a short whole-group minilesson that names a target, models the reading move in a brief model text, and moves quickly into guided application.
Transfer each modeled strategy into small-group, conference, and independent reading so children apply it in books they can sustain.
Use formative observation every day, plus weekly and unit assessments, to adjust scaffolding without turning one score into a verdict on a child.
Revisit model texts across a week for comprehension, vocabulary, structure, craft, and evidence, then synthesize learning through reflection and a unit inquiry project.
Treat culturally responsive perspectives and collaborative conversation as part of meaning-making, not as decoration around the reading task.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark content-rich reading workshop
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A comprehension workshop that builds knowledge and vocabulary through thematic model texts, brief explicit minilessons, guided practice, independent transfer, collaborative talk, formative observation, and recurring synthesis.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Organize reading around a three-week content theme and essential question. Model one comprehension, text-structure, vocabulary, or author-craft move in a short model text for 10 to 12 minutes. Guide immediate practice, then transfer the move into small-group, conference, or independent reading. Revisit texts across the week, reinforce vocabulary, collect daily observations, reflect with the child, and use weekly and unit evidence to decide what to model or scaffold next. Preserve parent judgment and accessible text choice rather than forcing a fixed reader level.

knowledgeBankGaps.title: Benchmark Grade 2 reading workshop format
knowledgeBankGaps.summary: A 10-unit, 30-week Grade 2 sequence with 15 daily minilessons per unit, unit essential questions, model-text rereading, independent reading, vocabulary micro-workshops, observations, weekly checks, unit assessments, and inquiry projects.
knowledgeBankGaps.content: Plan ten three-week units. Each unit opens with its content theme, essential question, text set, and research project. Across 15 daily minilessons, alternate comprehension strategies, genre, vocabulary and word relationships, text structure, author purpose, evidence, poetry or drama, comparison, and synthesis. Each minilesson follows the source's learning target, focus, model, guided practice, transfer, observation, and share rhythm. Reserve about 30 minutes for independent or supported reading when stamina permits, with a 15 to 20 minute bridge while stamina is developing. Offer a seven-minute vocabulary micro-workshop, weekly checks after Weeks 1 and 2, and a unit assessment and project close after Week 3.

layer3_structure.cadence: Five minilessons per week for 30 weeks, organized as 10 units of three weeks and 15 minilessons. The broader daily reading block combines read-aloud or shared reading, a 10 to 12 minute whole-group minilesson, small-group or independent reading, observation or conferencing, and a brief share and reflection. An optional seven-minute vocabulary micro-workshop reinforces unit language.

layer3_structure.weeklyTemplate: Day 1 of each unit launches the content theme, essential question, reading choices, and inquiry project. The remaining days cycle through a short model-text focus, explicit modeling, guided oral or notebook practice, a transfer bridge into small-group or independent reading, formative observation, and share or reflection. Vocabulary and word relationships recur on Days 4, 8, and 12 in this analysis because those are the unit's recurring vocabulary-focused minilessons. Week 1 and Week 2 may close with a weekly assessment. Week 3 compares texts, reads the unit poem, synthesizes the essential question, completes the inquiry project, and may close with the unit assessment.
layer3_structure.progressionModel: Linear 10-unit thematic progression with a repeated gradual-release lesson architecture. Comprehension strategies, genre, vocabulary, text structure, evidence, point of view, and author craft recur in increasingly varied literary, informational, dramatic, poetic, scientific, civic, historical, and economic texts.
layer3_structure.reviewRhythm: The same model texts are reread for different purposes across several days. Children then apply the move in independent reading, discuss and reflect on use, revisit vocabulary in a seven-minute micro-workshop, receive observation-informed support, and synthesize the three-week theme through comparison, a poem, an investigation project, and assessment.
studyRoutines: Preview the unit theme and essential question, then keep both visible while reading across the three weeks.
Read or listen to a short model text, name the day's reading move, and watch the parent model it aloud.
Practice together in the model text, then use the same move in a self-selected or parent-selected independent book.
Record a brief response in the reader's notebook and share evidence from the text.
Revisit unit vocabulary through context, roots and affixes, word relationships, reference tools, and the optional micro-workshop.
Use the parent observation record and weekly evidence to choose the next scaffold, book, or conference focus.
layer3_structure.bookAndReaderUse: Each unit supplies a short model-text collection and a poem, alongside interactive read-aloud and shared-reading suggestions. Children also read self-selected or teacher-selected independent books for sustained practice. In a homeschool adaptation, Homa should preserve the named model-text purpose but may substitute legally available, accessible books on the same theme when the source text is not licensed for delivery.
layer3_structure.homeschoolAdaptation: Keep the instructional sequence and evidence bar, but translate classroom grouping literally: whole group becomes parent and child, partner talk becomes parent-child or sibling talk, small group becomes one-to-one guided reading, and independent reading stays independent. The parent keeps authority over text fit, pacing, stopping, and assessment use.

activityTypes.description: Short prompts ask the learner to explain an idea, answer with evidence, and connect the response to the essential question.
A compact notebook page captures the day's target, text evidence, vocabulary, reflection, and independent-reading transfer.
Context, reference tools, roots and affixes, compounds, synonyms, antonyms, homographs, and shades of meaning reinforce unit vocabulary.
The parent records strategy use, evidence, fluency, independence, and needed scaffolds during guided and independent reading.
activityTypes.notes: The shared recipe owns the observation surface only. It must not invent pass lines, reading levels, diagnoses, or promotion decisions.

activityTypes.description: A three-week inquiry connected to the essential question supports planning, gathering evidence, organizing findings, and sharing a final product.
Optional Week 1, Week 2, and end-of-unit checks combine comprehension, vocabulary, and text-evidence tasks with the parent's observation record.
activityTypes.notes: Exact scoring, answer keys, age fit, and any progression decision must be deterministic and source-grounded. The recipe provides the printable bundle, not assessment policy.

activityTypes.description: Unit poems and dramatic scenes support oral rereading, expression, dialogue, imagery, rhyme, rhythm, repetition, and collaborative interpretation.

notes: A complete 11-file, 944-page Spanish Grade 2 reading workshop: 103 pages of overview and setup followed by ten three-week unit guides in exact source order. Carolyng specifically asked for study routines, weekly and daily breakdown, vocabulary reinforcement, books and readers, questions, guided and independent practice, observation and assessment, and subject matter across Units 1 through 10. Layers 1 through 5 now answer each request, and Layer 5 indexes all 150 daily minilessons rather than sampling weeks. The source is classroom-authored, so the homeschool adaptation preserves parent authority and converts grouping structures without pretending every home has a class. Both method contributions are active in production, all taxonomy proposals are resolved against the full live taxonomy, and Carolyng's explicit signals are recorded in Homa taste. Source text and model works remain off-repo except for the ignored sidecar and durable Blob originals.
